title: Merca's positivity conjecture for truncated Jacobi theta series
statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be integers with $1\le S<R/2$, and let $k\ge1$. Consider the theta series

$$
\frac{(-1)^k}{(q^S;q^R)_\infty(q^{R-S};q^R)_\infty}\sum_{j\ge k}(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)R/2-jS}(1-q^{(2j+1)S}).
$$

**Merca's conjecture.** This theta series has non-negative coefficients. The conjecture refines the established positivity theorem for averaged truncations of Jacobi's triple product identity; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
references:
**10 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.27507](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27507), [arXiv:2606.24243](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24243), [arXiv:2509.06357](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06357), [arXiv:2411.13818](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13818), [arXiv:2409.19907](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19907), [arXiv:2408.09467](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09467), [arXiv:2403.11608](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11608), [arXiv:2401.04019](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04019), [arXiv:2005.03619](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.03619).
